security_audit.summary: The Ruby backtick and hardcoded URL findings are Markdown documentation false positives, not hidden execution or suspicious network calls. remediation.suggestion: Package and audit the shared Google Workspace guidance with this skill, or inline the required auth and safety rules.
Require explicit user confirmation before using endActiveConference, patch, or other methods that change meeting state.
Document that commands require an installed, authenticated gws CLI and validated parameters from gws schema.

content.value_statement: Google Meet administration often requires precise CLI calls and API parameter discovery. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Meet resources with safer workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to call gws meet resources and methods.
Supports conference record lookup and listing workflows.
Covers participants, recordings, smart notes, and transcripts subresources.
Covers Meet space creation, lookup, update, and active conference ending.
Directs users to inspect method schemas before building parameters.
limitations: Requires the gws CLI to be installed and authenticated.
Depends on Google Meet API permissions granted to the active account.
Does not join meetings or create calendar invitations.
Requires a shared Google Workspace guidance file for full safety rules.

use_cases.title: Audit Meet Activity
use_cases.description: List recent conference records and review available meeting assets for compliance or support tasks.

use_cases.title: Prepare Meeting Follow-up
use_cases.description: Find recordings, transcripts, participants, and smart notes after an important meeting.

use_cases.title: Build Meet Automation
use_cases.description: Inspect gws schemas and plan safe API calls before integrating Meet workflows.

prompt_templates.title: List Recent Conferences
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gws Meet skill to list recent conference records. Show meeting names, start times, and available recordings.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Method
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the schema for spaces.get. Explain the required parameters before making any Meet API call.

prompt_templates.title: Review Meeting Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the conference record for my meeting. Summarize available participants, recordings, transcripts, and smart notes.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Space Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect spaces.patch. Draft the parameter plan, ask for confirmation, then update the meeting space only after approval.

output_examples.input: List conference records from the last week.
output_examples.output: Recent meetings: Weekly planning, Customer onboarding, and Design review. Each entry includes start time and available follow-up assets.

output_examples.input: Check whether a meeting has transcripts.
output_examples.output: The meeting has a transcript and smart notes. The response names the conference record and available follow-up resources.

output_examples.input: Prepare to end an active conference.
output_examples.output: Confirmation needed. This action can terminate a live meeting, so the skill identifies the target space and waits for approval.

best_practices: Inspect the gws schema before passing parameters to any Meet method.
Confirm the target meeting space before changing or ending a conference.
Use the least privileged Google account that can complete the task.
anti_patterns: Do not run state-changing methods without explicit user approval.
Do not assume a conference record ID from a meeting title alone.
Do not expose transcripts, recordings, or participant data in public channels.

faq.question: Does this skill require Google authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It relies on the gws CLI and Google Workspace credentials configured outside the skill.

faq.question: Can it create Meet spaces?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents the spaces create method through the gws meet command family.

faq.question: Can it manage recordings and transcripts?
faq.answer: It can inspect conference record subresources for recordings, transcripts, participants, and smart notes.

faq.question: Does it join meetings?
faq.answer: No. It manages Google Meet API resources and does not act as a meeting participant.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should destructive actions be confirmed?
faq.answer: Yes. Ending active conferences or updating meeting spaces should require explicit user confirmation.
